sources.title: Process Management Software
supportedClaims: The vendor page describes a level-one process map grouped into management, customer-facing, core and support categories and a level-two flowchart for each process.
The page describes named process owners and links from processes to controlled documents and standard clauses.
The page describes industry starting templates and review of supported PDF process charts before acceptance.
The vendor maps the module to ISO 9001:2015 clauses 4.4 and 5.3; this mapping is not proof that software alone satisfies requirements.

The page presents numbered configuration activities including process mapping, module configuration, standards onboarding and deployment with training. Details and applicability require demonstration.
The page states AI output is a suggestion reviewed by a person before entry into a controlled record.
These are published vendor descriptions, not verified installed behavior or proof of a particular plant’s conditions.

sources.title: ISO 9001 Auditing Practices Group
supportedClaims: The ISO 9001 Auditing Practices Group site provides educational papers on quality management system auditing, including a process-based approach and risk-based thinking.
The site says its guidance is not definitive and is not intended as specified requirements, a benchmark or mandatory audit criteria.
Its ISO 9001:2015 auditing topics include processes, evidence collection, audit planning and improvement.

evidence.text: The vendor's [top-level map description](https://isocertificationconsultants.ca/solutions/processes/) can be a useful demonstration starting point. Ask whether the organization can show its own boundaries and open a flowchart from an appropriate process. Ask who can change the grouping and how a reader knows which map is current. Record the answers as vendor statements or demonstrated behavior, not as a guarantee that every configuration is available.
The vendor page describes a level-one process map grouped into management, customer-facing, core and support categories and a level-two flowchart for each process.
The page describes named process owners and links from processes to controlled documents and standard clauses.

The [ICC page](https://isocertificationconsultants.ca/solutions/processes/) describes controlled documents and standard clauses linked to processes. Ask the vendor to demonstrate a process-to-document link using a sample chosen by the plant. Then ask what happens when that document is revised, withdrawn, or temporarily unavailable. The published description is a starting point for the test; it does not establish the behavior of every revision or permission scenario.
The page describes named process owners and links from processes to controlled documents and standard clauses.

Access also needs an explicit decision. The people who consult a map may not be the same people who edit it or approve changes. Ask who can view, propose, review, and release a change, and how those decisions are recorded. The [public description of a named owner](https://isocertificationconsultants.ca/solutions/processes/) is not evidence of a particular permission model, so treat permission detail as an evaluation question until demonstrated.
The page describes named process owners and links from processes to controlled documents and standard clauses.
These are published vendor descriptions, not verified installed behavior or proof of a particular plant’s conditions.
